## Intent
Hypothesis: Halide-expressible branchless blend with per-particle hash RNG enables compiler vectorization to approach the streaming ceiling.

## Cache saturation
Working set (68·N) spills L1d at N≈963 and L2 at N≈61680; all measured N (10000–10000000) are past L1d. At death_q=0.01, cost FALLS monotonically from 8.483 ns/p (N=10000) to 7.568 ns/p (N=10000000) — no knee at the L2→DRAM transition, just steady overhead amortization. At death_q=0.5 the curve is FLAT at ~7.5 ns/p across all N, confirming the shape is overhead-dominated, not cache-dominated. Higher death rate lowers the floor (7.568→7.559 at N=10M) and flattens N-dependence, suggesting dead particles skip the pixel-write inner loop.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 9.07 GB/s at N=10000, death_q=0.5 — 30% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. At death_q=0.01 the algo reaches 8.99 GB/s at N=10000000. The algo is compute-bound throughout: xctrace shows 76.8–88.8% compute cycles with backend stalls (9.6–17.6%) never dominating. No bandwidth-bound regime exists; bandwidth stays ~9 GB/s regardless of N because the bottleneck is scalar arithmetic and byte-granular pixel writes. Higher death_q slightly raises bandwidth (8.02→9.07 GB/s at N=10000) because dead particles skip pixel writes.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize. Only 2 vector-suffixed instructions appear — both `movi.2d` zero-initializations before a `bl _halide_b2` call (Halide RNG setup, not inlined). The hot loop uses scalar `s`-register ops: `ldp s4, s5`, `fadd s4`, `fmul s4`, `fcvtzs`, `fcmp`, `csel`. Pixel writes are byte-granular: `ldrb w2, [x1]`, `add w2, w2, w12`, `csel w2, w2, w11, lo`, `strb w2, [x1]`, repeated for three RGB channels. No `ld1` gather, no `fmul.4s`. Scalar arithmetic and `strb` byte stores explain the 30% ceiling — one component at a time, no SIMD width.

## Verdict
Refuted — achieved bandwidth never exceeds 9.07 GB/s (30% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling) because the compiler emitted scalar-only code with no vectorization (2 `movi.2d`, no `fmul.4s` or `ld1`), and byte-granular `strb` pixel writes cannot stream. The branchless blend kept branch flushes low (0.5–3.6%) but did not enable vectorization, so the hypothesis fails across all regimes.
